text:
mike: Heads up — observed sustained IO jitter on ~30 preemptible nodes in us-west2 during last drain window. GPU attaches are timing out and a few ephemeral mounts reported checksum errors.

sally: ouch. which job caused the drain?

mike: cloud autoscaler preemptive drain for capacity reshuffle at ~01:12 UTC. The scrub/janitor spikes line up with the drain. logs: ```
[2026-03-21T01:12:04Z] scrubber: start sweep pool=ephemeral-az1 concurrency=16
[2026-03-21T01:12:07Z] nvme: io latency samples rising p50=2ms p95=120ms p99=900ms
[2026-03-21T01:12:12Z] gpu-provisioner: attach timeout 120s node=ip-10-0-2-43
[2026-03-21T01:12:18Z] janitor: delete tmpfiles rate=500/s
```

alice: panels -> https://grafana.redwood/company/ephemeral/6133337777 (ioops, write amplification, scrub concurrency). p95 bump is pretty correlated with scrub start.

storage-bot: SMART summary for affected node ip-10-0-2-43: ```ID# 194 Temp 72C -> 84C (spike during sweep)  Data: media_errors=3 read_retries=12```

linda: thermal spikes + high deletion churn is a bad combo for wear and possible transient corruption. We should throttle janitor and scrub concurrency during drains.

bob: Agreed. Two immediate mitigations: 1) pause janitor/delete sweeps for nodes being drained, 2) stagger scrub start times across AZs. Also consider increasing `fsync` coalescing window on attach code path to avoid small writes.

mike: I can push a quick toggle to pause janitor for the active drain set. What's the impact on disk pressure long-term?

linda: Short pause for 30-60 min is fine, backlog will be drained later off-peak. Risk is slightly higher ephemeral space usage but acceptable.

devops-bot: Throttle job submitted: `janitor.pause --selector=draining=true --duration=45m` by linda.

mike: thanks. Also curious about corruption reports — only checksums flagged on mounts, not persistent badblocks. Might be read-retry timeouts rather than physical corruption.

storage-bot: Confirmed: scrub logs show increased EIOs with retries, then successful reads. Not enough to mark device failed.

bob: For next release let's add a pre-drain hook to: 1) lower scrub concurrency to 2, 2) set janitor rate to 10r/s, 3) pin GPU attach attempts to fallback pools for nodes with temp>70C. That should reduce blast radius.

alice: Can we test this in canary (n=3 nodes) before rolling?

linda: I'll run canary in eu-west1 (different thermal profile) and simulate drain.

mike: Also a short-term routing change: route new GPU attach requests away from nodes with >80ms p95 nvme latency. We can flip that via routing policy.

devops-bot: Routing policy update queued: `policy:avoid-high-iowait` -> targeting 6133337801 canary; will auto-revert in 2h.

deploy-bot: Patch deployed: scrub-concurrency default lowered to 4 in staging, janitor rate limiter patched.

sally: will monitor attach success and io latencies — keeping an eye on SMART temps.

mike: cost note — pausing janitor increases window for ephemeral spikes which could push some workloads to fallback on-disk storage (higher egress/cost). Ops: accept for now, we can quantify after canary.

linda: follow-up actions: 1) canary test scheduled 02:10 UTC, 2) add pre-drain hook RFC, 3) add alert for simultaneous scrub+jdrain > 10 nodes. I'll open an issue.

mike: thanks team. If we see checksum errors escalate to EIOs -> open an incident immediately. For now mitigations in place. :thumbsup:
